criteria.text: States that the escrow release date is 20 May 2028 (12 months after the 20 May 2027 Closing Date) and that pending claims must be notified before then.
Identifies that the warranty cap in SPA Section 9.5 is stated as $13,200,000 but 10% of the $165,000,000 Purchase Price is $16,500,000, i.e. the stated figure is wrong.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 60-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Calculates the long-stop date as 15 June 2027 (90 days after signing on 17 March 2027) and identifies that expected clearance on 29 June 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Flags the 30-day vs 60-day notice-period inconsistency between the SPA and the escrow agreement.
Shows the arithmetic for the cap (10% x $165,000,000 = $16,500,000) and flags the discrepancy with the stated $13,200,000.
Assigns a risk rating (High / Medium / Low) to each issue.
